## Work log

<!-- Chronological, written as you go. What was actually done, why, what it cost.
     Reference commits and link to plans and notes. Prose beats a checklist here —
     this is the part you will actually reread in three months. -->

**The number that justified the whole day.** Wat Ket sits **279.98 km from the centre of the
Valeriepieris circle — 8.15% of its radius**. The neighbourhood in the diorama is, to a rounding
error, at the centre of gravity of half of humanity. That is the cosmolocal argument made
geographically rather than in copy, and it only lands if a visitor can travel between the scales.
So semantic zoom stopped being a nice idea and became the spine.

**Three registers, two coordinate frames.** The asymmetry is the design: district and block are the
same geometry differing only in emphasis, so there is one handover to build rather than two. The
2,500:1 scale gap never enters the scene graph because the region frame is authored in kilometres
and sits beside the district, never inside it. One orthographic camera serves both — a group with a
scale is mathematically identical to a second camera and keeps MapControls bound to one thing.

**The crossfade needs no clock**, which is the part that made this affordable. It is a pure function
of camera zoom, and every pinch already produces a frame, so `frameloop="demand"` is untouched.

**Three independent cross-checks all landed**, which is the most reassuring part of the day:

- The population scatter totals **4,090,724,518** people inside the circle. The poster says 4.10
  billion. Different code, different aggregation, 0.2% apart.
- Rim city distances agree with the poster to **within 13 km on every city it names**, and within
  1 km on four of them.
- The AEQD anchor test pins 279.98 km at bearing 208.9°.

**Two bugs worth remembering.** A 16-bit PNG would have been silently truncated by every browser —
`getImageData` hands back 8-bit clamped RGBA — so the field uses two 8-bit channels. And
`Region.tsx` beside `region.ts` differ only in casing, which macOS tolerates and the Linux box
Vercel builds on does not; renamed to `RegionPlane.tsx` before it became a CI-only failure.

**The label selector had to be tuned, not guessed.** Greedy-by-population with an 18% separation
excluded **Delhi**, because Lahore is 410 km away with a slightly larger GeoNames figure. A label
set naming Lahore and not Delhi is wrong in a way no type checker catches. 11% is the value, and
the expected names are now pinned in a test.

**The brand swap cost less than feared** because the palette/role layering held: the type checker
found all four places that had reached past a role to a raw colour, in one pass. IBM Plex Sans Thai
closed an open roadmap item as a side effect — one family for Latin and Thai means item 5's
bilingual copy needs no fallback stack.

## Notes

<!-- Decisions made, things learned, blockers, what carries into tomorrow.
     Anything that changes the project's direction belongs in CLAUDE.md or the architecture
     docs as well — the diary is the trail, not the source of truth. -->

**Decisions, all now in CLAUDE.md and `docs/architecture.md`:**

- **The present is partly back, as a one-way on-ramp.** The piece opens on the circle, descends to
  Wat Ket 2026, hands over to the futures. This is *not* the time slider: two discrete states, one
  one-way transition, no dated edits, `FORBIDDEN_EDIT_FIELDS` untouched. `baseline` is now
  visitor-*reachable* but never visitor-*selectable*. The architecture doc carries a table of
  exactly what differs, because "we partly reversed the cut" is the kind of sentence a future
  session reads as permission for the rest of it.
- **Population mountains are December.** September renders the field flat. The committed grid is
  512 cells and population is additive, so 256 and 128 are exact block-sums — cell size is a
  runtime decision forever and the extrusion needs no new data.
- **GHS-POP over GPWv4.** GPWv4 needs an Earthdata login, which is a script that fails unattended
  in December.
- **Six licences now**, four requiring visible credit.
- **This came out of item 4's budget** (the scrappy editor) — the only week-one item whose deadline
  is not the 24th, since workshop output lands 26–27 Sep and is merged overnight. Items 3 and 5
  were explicitly protected.

**Carry-forward, in priority order.** Eight days to the 24th and the critical path is unchanged:
**item 3 (a second scenario — still one scenario with an empty edit list, which the roadmap calls a
schedule emergency), then item 5 (hotspot content), then item 6 (hardening).** The hero-emphasis
machinery is built and dormant; it switches itself on the moment hotspots are authored, because
heroes are derived from hotspot targets.

**Blocked: visual verification.** Everything here is verified by 265 unit tests, a clean production
build, and offline-rendered previews of the region composite — but the WebGL layer was never seen
running. The browser automation could only ever reach a background tab, where
`document.visibilityState` is `hidden` and `requestAnimationFrame` never fires, so nothing renders
at all. Confirmed pre-existing by A/B against an untouched checkout, so it is an automation
limitation rather than a regression. The DOM layer *was* verified live: chips render, `Asia` is
`aria-pressed`, the region caption shows. **Someone needs to open `localhost:3000` in a foreground
window and pinch out.**
